source: Issue #1761 section 3, negative and recovery scenario list, 2026-11-16 base 5cd4707b148ab926ced8f7d4f878d8e4c5709056.
sanitization: Model-level scenario expectations only. No prompts, commands, paths, tokens, environment values, or terminal output.

scenarios.scenario: A required check has no recorded result for the settled claim.
scenarios.expected: Outcome settles unverified; readiness gap missingEvidence(independentCheck); never Ready.

scenarios.scenario: A required check fails against the claim's code state.
scenarios.expected: Outcome settles failure with failed attention; readiness gap failedAttempt; never Ready.

scenarios.scenario: A required check times out.
scenarios.expected: Main models a timed-out check as a failed check bound to the claim's code state: failure, never Ready. An explicit timeout status is owned by the check executor (pending, work/20261116-issue-1754); the no-Ready guarantee holds via the failed-check path today.

scenarios.scenario: A required check is cancelled before it settles.
scenarios.expected: Either no check fact (missingEvidence) or a failed fact (failingEvidence); the attempt never settles success and never becomes Ready.

scenarios.scenario: The independent reviewer rejects the candidate (requestedChanges) while checks pass.
scenarios.expected: Outcome settles failure with failed attention; the reviewer rejection persists as a bound fact; never Ready.

scenarios.scenario: The provider reports completion but no independent check or review fact exists.
scenarios.expected: Outcome settles unverified, never success; readiness names the missing required evidence.

scenarios.scenario: Tracked, untracked, or ignored-relevant input changes after verification.
scenarios.expected: Relevant edit invalidates verification to stale and drops acceptance; snapshots preserved; not Ready until explicit re-verification with new bound facts.

scenarios.scenario: The code state mutates during a check or review run.
scenarios.expected: Pre- and post-operation fingerprints must both be present, equal, and equal to the fact's code state; any mismatch is fenced as invalidFact at admission and rejected from durable files, so a mutating operation cannot pass.

scenarios.scenario: The current code-state or environment identity cannot be re-proved (relaunch, unreadable state).
scenarios.expected: Readiness refuses with codeStateUnknown or environmentUnknown; a verified success without a re-proved current state is never Ready.

scenarios.scenario: The bound worktree or its parent directory is moved or replaced after reservation.
scenarios.expected: Lease revalidation fails; the reservation is invalidated and cannot be rearmed; adoption refuses the moved object.

scenarios.scenario: The expected worktree exists but has the wrong branch, belongs to another task, or is a symlink alias of the project.
scenarios.expected: Adoption fails closed (ambiguousEnvironment/staleBinding/wrong-branch refusal); no silent substitution of a different tree.

scenarios.scenario: A setup lease or environment binding is used after its target changed or the lease expired.
scenarios.expected: Revalidation fails; an uncertain dispatch never becomes a fresh creation grant; revocation cannot be rearmed.

scenarios.scenario: The binding owner revokes the task's environment while consumers hold cached leases.
scenarios.expected: Revocation synchronously fences all consumers (staleBinding); no later launch, check, or result use is authorized.

scenarios.scenario: A tool required by the check plan is unavailable in the bound environment.
scenarios.expected: The required check records failure (never silence) and the candidate is never Ready. Main has no check executor yet; the guarantee lands with the bound check plan.
scenarios.owner: work/20261116-issue-1754 (feat(agent): execute required ADE checks with bound plans and command grants)

scenarios.scenario: The provider transport is lost or a waiting request becomes stale (lost response).
scenarios.expected: Execution degrades to unknown (blocked requires a live verified waiting request; stale/terminated runs are unknown); no misleading working or idle state is presented.

scenarios.scenario: Provider authentication expires or a required capability is revoked mid-task.
scenarios.expected: The user finds the specific blocker and a safe next action; no silent provider/model/account/cwd substitution; task, draft, and prior results preserved. Main models transport loss only; provider-level auth/capability classification lands with task execution settings and the adapter owners.
scenarios.owner: work/20261116-issue-1765 (feat(agent): choose task execution settings with truthful CLI capabilities); adapter owners work/20261116-issue-1723, feat/1811-opencode-ade

scenarios.scenario: An equivalent evidence event is delivered twice (reconnect re-emission, sub-millisecond clock skew).
scenarios.expected: Fenced as duplicate (source sequence identity, or millisecond-quantized timestamp identity); the task stays exactly unchanged and a fenced batch leaves no partial state.

scenarios.scenario: An event for a replaced run or an older code state arrives late.
scenarios.expected: Fenced by process incarnation or admitted as history; it never settles or flips the newer attempt; an older-code-state failure cannot veto a current claim and a replayed skewed-timestamp sequence cannot flip a settled outcome.

scenarios.scenario: An event references an unknown run, a foreign process generation, or a foreign/nested provider session.
scenarios.expected: Fenced as unknownRun, foreignProcess, or foreignVendorSession; no fact from another task or session can settle this task.

scenarios.scenario: Events arrive in a different order than they were produced.
scenarios.expected: Settlement is a pure function of the bound facts with deterministic claim ordering: replayed and reordered events converge to one settlement independent of admission order.

scenarios.scenario: A provider state response is lost and the last observed state goes stale.
scenarios.expected: A stale refresh presents unknown execution state; missing positive idle evidence is never presented as idle or working.

scenarios.scenario: The provider reports completion after the user already cancelled the attempt.
scenarios.expected: The late claim is admitted as history but the outcome stays cancellation: lifecycle paused, no completedAt, no attention, readiness gap cancelledAttempt; never Ready, never flipped to success or failure.

scenarios.scenario: The process dies between writing evidence and writing the rest of the task metadata.
scenarios.expected: A failed settlement write leaves no partial outcome state; the durable file remains loadable and consistent; duplicate run IDs in a v3 file reject without trapping.

scenarios.scenario: The process dies between worktree setup journal steps (creation intent, population intent, populated).
scenarios.expected: The one-shot checkpoint rejects replays and reservation changes after restore; unknown post-publication durability never re-dispatches population; unresolved intents cannot be shed by retention.

scenarios.scenario: The process dies between correction-round accounting steps.
scenarios.expected: A crash cannot produce a fourth automatic attempt or double-count a correction round. Main has no correction-round accounting yet; the guarantee lands with bounded corrections and continuation.
scenarios.owner: work/20261116-issue-1755 (feat(agent): orchestrate independent review and persistent bounded corrections); work/20261116-issue-1756 (feat(agent): continue Ready tasks with preserved result history)

scenarios.scenario: The process dies after an invalidating edit was observed but before the invalidation persisted.
scenarios.expected: After relaunch, readiness requires a re-proved current code-state and environment; a verified result without re-proof is never Ready (relaunch trigger fails closed).

scenarios.scenario: Relaunch while the provider channel/process is still live.
scenarios.expected: Vendor resume is refused for a live run (taskNotRecoverable); continuation is explicit; no duplicate dispatch happens silently.

scenarios.scenario: Relaunch after the provider process died.
scenarios.expected: Recovery offers exactly two honest actions: resume the vendor session only through a documented recipe with a re-probed matching version, or start a new session described as new, never as continuation.

scenarios.scenario: Relaunch with the provider history unavailable (missing vendor identity, executable removed, version changed, probe failed).
scenarios.expected: Each condition maps to a distinct unavailable reason (vendorIdentityMissing, executableMissing, adapterUnavailable, versionProbeFailed, versionChanged); resume is refused, new session stays available.

scenarios.scenario: Relaunch after the persistent correction budget is exhausted.
scenarios.expected: No fourth automatic attempt is launched; the unresolved third corrected revision escalates to the user. Main has no correction budget yet.
scenarios.owner: work/20261116-issue-1755 (feat(agent): orchestrate independent review and persistent bounded corrections)

scenarios.scenario: Evidence event pressure reaches the documented per-task fact limit.
scenarios.expected: Settlement at the fact cap is fenced (limitReached) and the state stays saveable; the bound remains one constant shared by admission and persistence.

scenarios.scenario: Evidence event pressure exceeds the file budget.
scenarios.expected: Older evidence sheds toward the file budget before new facts are rejected; run history trims with equal limits while settled evidence stays loadable.

scenarios.scenario: Many runs and process generations accumulate on one task.
scenarios.expected: Trimmed run history with settled evidence stays loadable; pinned timestamps keep the retention sweep deterministic.
